<why>
All candidates A–E and G correctly conclude that the last drop is NOT a sufficient cause, which matches the standard philosophical answer. Candidate F uniquely argues YES, treating the tank's full state as a background condition making the drop sufficient—but this contradicts the standard logician's interpretation of "sufficient cause" (which must work in isolation). Among the NO answers, E contains a technical error in its INUS definition, stating "insufficient but necessary part" instead of Mackie's actual term "Non-redundant part." Candidate G is most accurate: it correctly defines INUS as "Insufficient but Non-redundant part of an Unnecessary but Sufficient condition," includes the instructive straw-that-broke-the-camel's-back analogy, maintains clear structure, and gives the logician's answer without embellishment. Candidate C is a close alternative—clearer on what the drop IS (triggering cause, actualizer)—but lacks the technical framework and analogy that a logician would recognize.
</why>
